newsitem.title: USA: Middlefield, Conn. to lose funds for sewer project.
newsitem.headline: Middlefield, Conn. to lose funds for sewer project.

text.p: A miscalculation by state environmental officials has resulted in $465,000 less in state grants for the proposed $7.6 million Lake Beseck sewer project, the Hartford Courant reported on Thursday.
If no new funding is found, a scheduled May 20 townwide referendum on the sewer project may have to be postpooned, the Courant reported.

The $7.6 million project would bring sewers to about 350 homes and businesses around the lake. The spending must be approved by a majority of town voters, even though residents in the proposed sewer area would be the only ones to pay. The system is needed to replace a failing septic system.
The governor's office has requested a $452,000 rural hardship grant from the federal government for the sewer project.
In December, the state Departmnent of Environmental Protection (DEP) said the sewer project would qualify for $1.26 million in grants and another $1.26 million in low-interest loans.
But state DEP officials did not take into account federal grants and low-cost loans to the project when figuring out what state funding the project was eligible to receive, the Courant reported.
As a result, DEP officials notified the town earlier this month that the grant amount would be reduced by $465,000; and the amount in loans would be reduced by $286,000.
